audience.text: Python developers building applications that require generating Code 128, Code 39, EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, UPC-E, and QR Code barcodes without system-level dependencies beyond Pillow.

capabilities.text: Supports Code 128 (with automatic or forced encode mode), Code 39/Code 39 Extended, EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, and UPC-E.
capabilities.title: Generate multiple linear symbologies

capabilities.text: Encodes QR Code Model 2 versions 1–40 with selectable error correction level and encoding mode.
capabilities.title: Generate QR Code with configurable options

capabilities.text: Produces SVG via `to_svg()` returning a string, and PNG via `to_png()` returning bytes.
capabilities.title: Render barcodes to SVG and PNG

capabilities.text: Uses `RenderOptions` to configure scale, DPI, module width/height, quiet zone, colors, text display, and font.
capabilities.title: Control rendering appearance

capabilities.text: Allows rendering through `SvgRenderer`, `PngRenderer`, or `PdfRenderer` instances via `Barcode.render()`.
capabilities.title: Support custom renderers

limitations.text: PDF rendering is not implemented; `Barcode.to_pdf()` and `PdfRenderer.render()` raise `NotImplementedError`.
The library only generates barcodes and does not read or decode existing barcode images.
ECI normalization and validation are not implemented despite `EncodeOptions.eci_assignment_number` being exposed.
GS1 data parsing and validation are not implemented despite `EncodeOptions.gs1_enabled` being exposed.

problems_solved.text: Provides a pure-Python, dependency-light solution for generating multiple barcode symbologies with deterministic output.
Enables flexible barcode rendering to SVG and PNG formats with configurable options.
Supports both dedicated helper functions and a generic `generate()` entry point for selecting symbologies.
Allows fine-grained control over rendering through `RenderOptions` and custom `Renderer` subclasses.

product_summary.text: Aspose.BarCode FOSS for Python is a pure-Python, open-source library for generating deterministic, standards-compliant linear and 2D barcodes.

uncertainties: The exact set of symbology aliases supported by `generate()` is not explicitly listed in the facts.
Whether `Ean13Options`, `Ean8Options`, `UpcaOptions`, and `UpceOptions` support explicit check-digit input beyond automatic computation is not confirmed by examples.
The behavior of `ResolvedRenderOptions` and how it differs from `RenderOptions` is not demonstrated.
The scope of `aspose_barcode_foss.api` and `aspose_barcode_foss.result` modules is not shown in examples or public symbols.

workflows.name: Generate and render a Code 128 barcode
workflows.text: Import `code128`, create a barcode with `code128(payload)`, then call `to_svg()` or `to_png()` to produce output.

workflows.name: Select symbology generically
workflows.text: Use `generate(symbology_name, payload)` to create a barcode for any supported symbology by name.

workflows.name: Configure QR Code encoding options
workflows.text: Pass a `QrOptions` instance to `qr()` to set error correction level and encoding mode.

workflows.name: Add check digits or extended encoding
workflows.text: Use `Code39Options(add_check_digit=True)` or `code39ext()` to encode extended character sets.

workflows.name: Customize rendering appearance
workflows.text: Pass `RenderOptions` to `to_svg()` or `to_png()` to control scale, DPI, module width, text display, and colors.

workflows.name: Render using a specific renderer
workflows.text: Instantiate a `SvgRenderer`, `PngRenderer`, or `PdfRenderer`, then call `barcode.render(renderer, options=...)`.
